Iran's Foreign Minister Abbas Araqchi ‌and US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner communicated through mediators on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly in New York, the first such contacts since an interim ceasefire agreement collapsed in July.

# Iran's president tells Trump it will never 'bend the knee'

![](https://static.files.bbci.co.uk/bbcdotcom/web/20260907-085256-bea8b058c0-web-3.21.0/grey-placeholder.png)
![EPA Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian addresses the UN General Assembly in New York (23 September 2026)](https://ichef.bbci.co.uk/news/480/cpsprodpb/fe3f/live/8c85eb50-b766-11f1-b1d1-571ed4d7ff2c.jpg.webp)

President Masoud Pezeshkian has said Iran will never "bend the knee" after almost seven months of war with the US and Israel, but is ready for a diplomatic solution to the conflict.

Responding to US President Donald Trump's threat to "annihilate" the Islamic Republic if a deal is not reached soon, he told the UN General Assembly: "The resistance of the Iranian people will only increase in the face of sanctions, increased pressure, increased bullying."

Pezeshkian also insisted any deal would have to include an end to the US blockade stopping Iranian ships from using a key Gulf waterway.

"It cannot be the case that everyone benefits from the Strait of Hormuz while we are denied access," he said.

There was no immediate comment from the US, whose delegation walked out of the chamber at the start of Pezeshkian's address.

## [Pakistan must ‘catch up’ with India in T20 cricket, says coach Hesson](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/9/23/pakistan-must-catch-up-with-india-in-t20-cricket-says-coach-hesson)

   [![India-Pakistan Cricket](https://wordpress.aljazeera.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/02/AP26046548947819-1771175442.jpg?fit=1568%2C1045)](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2026/9/23/pakistan-must-catch-up-with-india-in-t20-cricket-says-coach-hesson)  

Head coach Mike Hesson has admitted that Pakistan will have some catching up to do if they are to challenge archrivals India at the Asian Games.

India’s men have won back-to-back Twenty20 World Cups and are also defending champions at the Asian Games.

Since Hesson took over in May last year, Pakistan have lost to India three times in the [Asia Cup 2025](https://www.aljazeera.com/sports/2025/9/28/india-defeat-pakistan-by-five-wickets-in-controversy-hit-asia-cup-final) and once in this year’s T20 World Cup.

“India are the benchmark in terms of white-ball cricket at the moment, and our challenge is to catch up to that,” said Hesson in Karachi before the team’s departure for Japan.

The men’s cricket at the Asian Games in Japan starts on Thursday.

Pakistan and India have never met at the games but are likely to face-off in the semifinals on October 1 in Nagoya.
